answer: A sparrow guards an agent economy with opal-pebble stacking: every new identity must stack opal pebbles in a pond-side nest, and each stack follows the tribonacci rule, so the first fake stacks 1 pebble, the second 1, the third 2, the tenth 149 and the twentieth 66,012, and twenty fakes together stack 144,664 pebbles. Bulk farming fails because one sparrow carries one pebble and each stack must be finished before the next begins, so no pebble can be stacked in parallel or bought; like ripples spreading one ring at a time across a still pond, never in bulk.
